newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: S.Korean yields close up on liquidity shortages.
newsitem.headline: S.Korean yields close up on liquidity shortages.

text.p: Bond yields closed higher for the third consecutive day on Thursday due to continuing liquidity shortages, dealers said.
The trading sentiment on corporate bonds was also affected by expectations that there would be more applications for next month's new issues than earlier expected, they said.
Overnight call rates also rose due to the short liquidity.
* 3-yr corporates close at 12.15 pct vs Tuesday's 12.07
* 3-mth CDs end at 13.65 pct vs Tuesday's 13.50
* Average overnight call rate at 15.3 pct vs 14.8
Dealers said the applications were estimated at 3.26 trillion won, compared with earlier forecasts of below three trillion.
Overnight call rates also rose to an average of 15.3 percent from 14.8 percent due to the liquidity shortage.
